_doc: DEWY receipts for 2026-08-17 — PRL 1.1 landing session (Sugar routing ground-truth investigation + web-form delivery diagnosis + prl.arcs.care/status/<seg> URL family). See _ARTIFACTS/prl-1-1-evidence/ for raw evidence and prl.arcs.care/status/{crm,troubleshooting} for the client-facing surfaces.

receipts.sharp_question: Does Todd's territory-map CSV actually match how Sugar routes leads today, and is it safe to build chatbot delivery on top of it?

dewy_vector.D: No. Full 43-state sandbox sweep (create-tagged-lead -> read assigned_user -> delete, lead_source=Chatbot) found ~49% mismatch vs the CSV: several states route to a different rep, every 'Distribution'-tagged state routes elsewhere (that category may correspond to no real Sugar rule), 2 active reps (Dan Damas, Tim Mulcahy) are missing from the CSV roster entirely, and 6 states plus all 7 states outside Sugar's location_c enum land with NO assigned owner at all (worse than misrouted — no queue catches it).
dewy_vector.E: Todd Hotes (client, decision owner), Bill Galla (Sugar owner + territory-map author, not yet looped in), Jorge/Josh (IT/site, out of scope for this finding)
dewy_vector.W: Live now — this same gap already affects real 'Web Site'-sourced leads today, confirmed by testing TX under both lead_source values with identical routing. Not introduced by the chatbot.

receipts.true_north: Neither the CSV nor Sugar's live behavior should be trusted as ground truth until Bill confirms which is right, state by state — build nothing that silently corrects toward either.
receipts.why: 1.1's delivery build was about to inherit routing logic from the CSV. Testing before wiring found the CSV itself was wrong roughly half the time, which would have shipped a chatbot that promises correct geo-routing while actually misrouting or dropping leads.
receipts.loki: Risk that the sandbox sample doesn't generalize to prod, or that Sugar's sandbox routing config diverges from prod. Mitigated by cross-checking prod's real 'Web Site'-sourced leads (independent evidence, same pattern) and by keeping the ask scoped to alignment, not a unilateral fix.
receipts.bar: High if ignored (silent lead loss/misroute at scale once chatbot traffic starts); low to de-risk (one 30-min call before building anything on the CSV).
receipts.horizon: Resolves once Bill confirms per-state ground truth on the proposed call.

receipts.sharp_question: Does location_c want state abbreviations or full names? Two prior 'verified' sources (today's pickup doc vs. an Aug-11 100-record prod audit) disagreed.

dewy_vector.D: Abbreviation is correct. Re-verified live: the enum schema defines US states as 2-letter keys; of 15 recent prod records, the 2 sourced via the existing automated 'Web Site' integration both used abbreviations, while the 'Other' (manual/bulk-import) records used full names. The Aug-11 doc's 'full names' finding was a sampling artifact — its 100-record snapshot was 91% manual 'Other' entries, the same skew that doc itself flagged for a different stat two paragraphs earlier.

receipts.true_north: When two 'verified' facts conflict, re-verify live against fresh evidence rather than picking a side — the resolution is often that one source's sampling was biased, not that either author was careless.
receipts.why: Writing the wrong format would have silently broken auto-routing for every state on the very field this session's larger finding is about.
receipts.loki: Low — resolved with primary evidence (schema + real automated-path records), not inference.

receipts.sharp_question: An unmerged branch (claude/chatbot-1-1-jtbd-blockers-edda33) turned out to already contain a capture-first Tidio flow design + a 22,500-case-verified recognizer test suite. Merge it, or rebuild from scratch?

dewy_vector.D: Selectively checkout just the relevant path (runtime/recoil/generated/prl-lyro/, 56 files) rather than a full git merge — the two branches had 117 vs 192 commits of unrelated drift since their fork point, so a full merge would have pulled in a large amount of irrelevant history. Re-ran the Layer-0 deterministic tests post-merge to confirm the code was live and correct, not stale, before trusting it.
dewy_vector.E: this repo's git history, future sessions reading it

receipts.true_north: Reuse existing, tested work over rebuilding — but verify it's still correct before trusting it, don't just take the file's word for it.
receipts.why: Closed most of leg 1's flow-mapping scope in one step instead of redoing work that already existed and was better-tested than what would have been rebuilt from scratch this session.
receipts.loki: Risk the merged code was stale/broken and would be trusted blindly. Mitigated: ran all Layer-0 self-tests post-merge (recognizer 34/34, coverage sweep, 22,500-case grid) before treating any of it as ground truth.

receipts.surface: PRL / web form delivery + comms sequencing
receipts.sharp_question: Gravity Forms doesn't deliver leads to Sugar. Jorge already has partial (different) context from an earlier Barracuda-quarantine fix. Fix it and loop Jorge in directly, or get Todd's sign-off on the approach first?

dewy_vector.D: Get Todd's sign-off first. The recommended fix (Sugar's native Web-to-Lead form, bypassing email/SMTP/Barracuda entirely) is a different mechanism than what Jorge already partially worked on, and neither Jorge nor Josh has any visibility into it. Stood up a dedicated status page (prl.arcs.care/status/troubleshooting) explaining both problems separately (email-notification vs. Sugar-delivery) and drafted (not sent) a summary email to Todd asking only for a nod before anything goes to Jorge/Josh.
dewy_vector.E: Todd (approval), Jorge (IT/DNS, partial context on the wrong half of the problem), Josh/Websites-For-Anything (likely owns the actual template-edit access needed)

receipts.true_north: Don't let a vendor/IT contact's partial context on an old fix stand in for the client's approval of a new, different fix — explain the plan to the decision-maker before it reaches the people who'd implement it.
receipts.why: Jorge's Aug-14 Barracuda fix addressed a real but narrower problem (notification email) than the actual finding (no Sugar delivery mechanism existed at all). Looping him in on the new fix without Todd's context first risked confusing two separate problems and building on an unapproved plan.
receipts.loki: Low — this just adds one approval step before outreach; no technical risk introduced.

receipts.sharp_question: Multiple PRL cross-workstream status pages are coming (CRM, web forms, Tidio, build). What URL pattern, and how to avoid the known beforeFiles re-catch bug this repo already has a name for?

dewy_vector.D: prl.arcs.care/status/<seg>, one entry per segment. Wired via proxy.ts MULTI_PATH_MAP as the deterministic primary mechanism (same pattern already proven for todd-call.arcs.care and julia.arcs.care), with next.config.ts carrying a capture-group backstop. First attempt used only the next.config.ts approach and shipped with the bug: the exclusion pattern tested the ORIGINAL request path for 'status/', but Vercel's beforeFiles rewrites re-run on a second pass against the REWRITTEN destination filename ('prl-status-crm.html', which contains 'status-' not 'status/'), so the fallback wildcard silently re-caught and overwrote the correct rewrite. Caught by curl header inspection (x-nextjs-rewritten-query showed the correct match; x-matched-path showed the wrong one), fixed by adding proxy.ts as primary + correcting the next.config.ts exclusion to match the destination substring.
dewy_vector.E: future sessions adding prl.arcs.care/status/* pages (tidio, wp, build reserved but not built)
dewy_vector.W: DURABLE pattern, now documented in code comments in both files.

receipts.true_north: When a codebase already has a documented bug class with a proven fix shape, apply the SAME fix shape exactly — don't half-apply it based on surface-level pattern matching.
receipts.why: This is the second time this exact bug class has bitten this repo (first for todd-call/julia, now for prl/status). The fix is now in the same proven shape both places, and the segment convention makes adding tidio/wp/build later a one-line change, not new config surgery.
receipts.loki: Caught the same day via direct curl verification rather than trusting the deploy log, which showed a successful build even though routing was silently wrong.

receipts.surface: PRL / Tidio -> Sugar delivery mechanism (1.1/1.2 chatbot-only scope)
receipts.sharp_question: Tidio's delivery leg was left open as 'API-call node (per prior research) vs. Zapier Catch Hook' — which one is actually buildable on PRL's current Tidio plan?

dewy_vector.D: Zapier Catch Hook. Confirmed by the client: PRL's Tidio account is not Pro/Growth tier, so Tidio's webhook/API-call node is not available on this plan. The prior 'API-call node should work per prior research' note was wrong for this account's actual tier and is superseded. This means the flows already imported/merged into this repo (runtime/recoil/generated/prl-lyro/tidio-flows/) will need manual modification to add a Zapier Catch Hook trigger step, and since no MCP tool creates a standing Catch Hook (trigger+public URL+action) headlessly, that hook has to be set up once, manually, in the Zapier web UI before the flow can call it.
dewy_vector.E: Todd/PRL Tidio account (plan-tier constraint), Zapier (manual one-time Catch Hook setup), next session (executes the flow edit)
dewy_vector.W: Blocks the 1.1/1.2 delivery-leg build until the Catch Hook exists — this is now the first concrete step of next session, not an open question.

receipts.true_north: Confirm plan-tier/feature availability against the actual account before designing a delivery mechanism around it — 'should work per prior research' is not the same as verified for this specific account.
receipts.why: Would have wasted the next session's build time attempting to wire a Tidio API-call node that doesn't exist on this plan; now the correct mechanism (Catch Hook) is locked in before that session starts.
receipts.loki: Low — this is a direct account-tier fact from the client, not inference.
receipts.horizon: Resolves once the Catch Hook is manually created and wired into the imported flow.

receipts.sharp_question: Once the sandbox Catch Hook delivery leg is wired, do we point it at prod (prlresins.sugarondemand.com) as part of the same build pass?

dewy_vector.D: No. Explicit client instruction: not touching prod yet. All 1.1/1.2 validate/confirm/verify work happens against the WP staging site + Sugar sandbox only. The prod lead_source enum question (does 'Chatbot' need a fallback value since it only exists in sandbox) stays an open item, not something to resolve by testing against prod directly.
dewy_vector.E: prlresins.sugarondemand.com (prod, untouched), prlresinstest.sugarondemand.com (sandbox, active), WP staging site (active)
dewy_vector.W: Holds until the client explicitly greenlights a prod cutover — do not initiate it proactively even after staging looks clean.

receipts.true_north: A clean staging/sandbox pass is not itself authorization to touch prod — that is always a separate, explicit go-ahead.
receipts.why: Prevents the next session from treating 'sandbox works' as license to also validate/fix the prod lead_source enum gap in the same pass, which the client did not ask for.
receipts.loki: Low — direct client instruction, not inference.

receipts.surface: PRL / Tidio -> Sugar delivery leg (1.1/1.2 chatbot-only scope)
receipts.sharp_question: Zapier co-pilot proposed 2 fixes (name-split, CA-fallback removal) against bugs found in live sandbox data. Dual bar-raiser protocol run: Claude as architect/advisor, Zapier co-pilot as implementing agent. Did both fixes actually land correctly, and is the Zap safe to publish?

dewy_vector.D: Yes, published (v0.4, series_376761228, sandbox-only). Both fixes independently verified by Claude via direct Sugar read (not trusting the co-pilot's self-reported Zapier step-test echo) against record 7b611d4c-9b3f-11f1-b848-0eb473bb02df (2026-08-18 20:00:38 UTC): last_name split correctly to 'O'Kon DDS' (title/suffix preserved, first token dropped per the agreed no-guessing rule), and a state-parse audit trail ('State parse: True | raw input: "..."') genuinely persisted in the description field. One real architectural correction made mid-build: location_c is a hard-required Sugar field, so neither 'empty string' nor 'omit the key' could ever work regardless of the enum listing an empty UI choice (confirmed: Sugar's required-field validation rejects empty string at the API layer even when the enum technically allows it in the UI) -- the fix had to keep a real fallback state code and make failures detectable via a SIBLING field (description) instead of trying to make the required field itself signal failure.
dewy_vector.E: Zapier co-pilot (implementing agent), Claude (architect/advisor -- verify, not trust), Todd (final real-conversation test still pending)
dewy_vector.W: Live in sandbox now. Blocked on: (1) one real Tidio staging conversation (everything verified so far is still a Zapier step-test replay, not an actual chat), (2) Bill's routing call, (3) production Chatbot enum + auth repoint -- all separately gated, none block this sandbox publish.

receipts.true_north: In a dual-agent bar-raiser protocol, the advisor's job is to independently re-verify the implementer's claimed fix against the actual system of record, not accept a step-test's self-reported success -- this caught nothing wrong here, but the discipline is what makes the sign-off meaningful rather than rubber-stamped.
receipts.why: A schema-breaking fix (empty/omitted required field) would have silently converted a lead-misrouting bug into a lead-loss bug, worse than the original problem. Independent verification before publish confirmed the actual correct redesign (sibling-field audit trail) instead of a plausible-sounding but broken one.
receipts.loki: Low -- every claim checked against a direct Sugar API read, not inference or trust in the co-pilot's report.
receipts.bar: Low, now that it's published to sandbox only.
receipts.horizon: Resolves fully once the real Tidio conversation test lands and is independently re-verified the same way.

receipts.surface: PRL / Tidio -> Sugar delivery leg (1.1/1.2 chatbot-only scope)
receipts.sharp_question: The last gap in the bar-raiser closure was a real (non-synthetic) conversation through WP staging, not a Zapier step-test replay. Does a genuine end-to-end run confirm the fixes hold outside the test harness?

dewy_vector.D: Yes. Real WP staging conversation produced Sugar Lead 435cee66-9b40-11f1-9cd7-02309379545d (2026-08-18 20:06:13 UTC), independently read (not self-reported): first_name/last_name split cleanly with real data ('Zach'/'Harris'), location_c correctly parsed to 'CT' (a real code, not the CA fallback), description carries the audit trail correctly showing 'State parse: False | raw input: "CT"' (False = parsed successfully, confirming the audit trail is symmetric and not just a failure-path artifact), lead_source='Chatbot' as intended. This is the first non-synthetic, non-replay record to complete the chain -- everything before this was either a Zapier step-test or Faker-generated data. 1.1/1.2 chatbot-only scope is now verified end-to-end in staging/sandbox.
dewy_vector.E: PRL / Todd, Tidio (live sandbox flow), Zapier (series_376761228), Sugar sandbox
dewy_vector.W: Closed for staging/sandbox. Production cutover remains separately gated (Bill's routing call, prod Chatbot enum, auth repoint) -- untouched, per explicit staging-only scope this session.

receipts.true_north: A test harness passing is not the same claim as the real system working -- the bar-raiser protocol's final gate was always the untestable-by-proxy case, and it held.
receipts.why: Closes the last open item from the 2026-08-18 Zap-publish receipt. 1.1/1.2 (chatbot -> Sugar delivery) is now genuinely done, not just published-and-hoped.
receipts.loki: Low -- independent Sugar read, real conversation, real data.
receipts.horizon: DURABLE for this scope. Production repoint is the next, separately-gated phase.

receipts.surface: PRL / Tidio trigger + Zap dedup integrity
receipts.sharp_question: Why did mobile visitors get Lyro's email ask instead of the flow, and is the dedup path safe for edge-case payloads?

dewy_vector.D: Trigger was 'Visitor returns to the site' — fresh visitors got NO flow and fell through to Lyro. Fixed live in Tidio (claude-in-chrome): replaced with 'Visitor clicks on chat icon', activated, mobile verified 1-1 with desktop. Separately, a real submission with an empty email made Find-Record match arbitrarily and Path A updated an unrelated REAL 2021 lead (Roger A Lamarre) — update-only fields wrote 'Not specified' title/industry and appended '— Updated via Chatbot' to description; the actual submission's data was lost. Fix (owed, co-pilot): Filter step requiring non-empty email before search; empty-email routes to create. Repair owed on the polluted record.
dewy_vector.E: Tidio flow 7701936, Zap 376827315, Roger A Lamarre record ea77a7d2 (polluted), Todd (was about to demo this)
dewy_vector.W: Trigger fix DONE. Dedup filter + record repair are next session's first work — before any more demo traffic.

receipts.true_north: A search-then-update path must never run on a possibly-empty key — an empty search term turns dedup into a random-record mutator, which is worse than duplicating.
receipts.why: Both bugs were found by verifying real behavior (fresh-visitor test; independent Sugar read after Zach's submission) rather than trusting the published config.
receipts.loki: Low on the trigger (verified live). Dedup bug evidenced by the polluted record itself.
receipts.bar: High until the filter ships — every empty-email submission can corrupt a real record. Sandbox-only today.
